anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: The database is simultaneously experiencing excessive lock contention and/or deadlocks in the lock manager, uncontrolled growth or exhaustion of engine-level memory regions, and physical corruption or logical inconsistency of on-disk data and index pages. All three root causes coexist during the same workload execution, creating a multifaceted failure mode that spans concurrency control, memory management, and storage integrity.

Combined observable phenomena: 1) Long blocker-waiter chains, frequent deadlock victim rollbacks, and sharp drops in transaction throughput. 2) Escalating resident-set size, swapping or OOM events, plummeting cache-hit ratios, and CPU stalls caused by memory pressure. 3) Intermittent corruption errors, checksum failures, and mismatched row counts between index and heap scans. Because the faults reinforce one another, operators may also see: transactions stuck in lock wait while holding large private work buffers that cannot be freed; corruption-induced plan fall-backs to full scans that inflate both lock footprints and memory consumption; node restarts triggered by combined OOM kills and corruption-related assertion failures; and a surge of application-side timeouts and retry storms that obscure the true root causes.

Causal interaction: Damaged data or index pages can force the optimizer to abandon narrow index paths in favor of broader scans, which lock more rows or pages for longer periods, heightening lock contention. These heavier scans also allocate larger buffer and work areas, accelerating memory exhaustion. In turn, severe memory pressure prolongs execution time, delays lock release, and may trigger automatic lock-escalation, all of which deepen blocking chains. Prolonged lock waits keep dirty or inconsistent pages pinned in shared buffers, hampering checkpoint flush and increasing the likelihood that corrupted pages survive or propagate. Repeated crash recoveries due to OOM or corruption amplify concurrency storms when clients reconnect, recreating the contention–memory–corruption cycle and progressively degrading the overall database health.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
